goalbuddy_receipt_v1.rationale: User-facing claim: Type, Select, Drag, and Hold are trustworthy canvas-first cues that remain adjustable through the shared durable/native path. T011 fixes exact Hold target coverage: two independently animated targets produce matching generated-track coverage, while mixed and missing-boundary scopes reject atomically. However, the new editor eligibility filter regresses Hold adjustment. After authoring a Hold, changing its enter time recomputes eligibility against cue-generated tracks; because the source tracks now live only in the cue replacement, all valid selected targets disappear and update becomes disabled. This blocks a valid boundary change despite the domain’s stored replacement supporting it. All other previously accepted evidence remains green, but T005 should not begin until this bounded UI defect is corrected.
evidence: Exact Hold target coverage — PASS: packages/domain/src/index.ts:1022-1028 now rejects when any semantic target lacks a source track; the replacement bundle then validates an explicit enter boundary for every included track at lines 1029-1047.

Genuine multi-target Hold — PASS: fixtures/public-synthetic/reusable-cues.html defines independent opacity and transform animations with explicit 1000 ms boundaries. Installed Chrome selects exactly those two targets and, after durable reload, asserts sorted semantic target IDs equal generated Hold track element IDs at apps/editor/tests/phase4-reusable-cues.spec.ts:71-79 and 134-141.

Fail-closed atomicity — PASS: packages/domain/src/cue-authoring.test.ts:267-292 rejects animated-plus-unanimated scope with CUE_HOLD_TARGET_UNANIMATED and missing-boundary scope with CUE_HOLD_ENTER_BOUNDARY_MISSING while canonical bytes and revision remain unchanged.

CLI parity — PASS: packages/motion-cli/src/cli.test.ts:204-222 exercises both invalid scopes through the service, receives the exact reason codes, confirms workspace revision remains 3 after each rejection, then successfully commits the valid two-target Hold at revision 4.
Initial editor eligibility — PASS: holdTargetOptions filters the initial Hold list through projectCueReplacement; installed Chrome asserts only the two eligible animated stable IDs are advertised.

Remaining P1 adjustment regression — apps/editor/src/main.ts:1577-1585 recognizes an attached Hold only when its existing enterMs equals the newly entered time. After creation, ordinary source tracks have been replaced by cue-owned generated tracks. Changing enter from 1000 ms to another valid stored-source boundary such as 0 ms makes projectCueReplacement inspect generated tracks, reject them as replacement input, and return no options.

The change listener at apps/editor/src/main.ts:432-435 immediately calls refreshHoldTargetOptions; lines 1589-1595 rebuild the select, cannot restore now-absent selected IDs, and rerender with the Hold submit disabled. The stored cue replacement would allow this valid update through packages/domain/src/index.ts:938-959, so the UI—not the domain contract—is the blocker.

No browser test edits an authored Hold’s enter boundary; the current green proof covers creation and exact coverage but cannot detect this regression. This contradicts the goal oracle’s requirement that the cue remain adjustable.
Previously accepted Drag evidence remains green: three-waypoint creation, direct intermediate-point drag, CLI round-trip, reload, timing edit, and exact undo/redo are still covered.

Keyboard, responsive, boundary, native-preview, reduced-motion, diagnostics, and history evidence did not regress: installed Chrome passed 1/1, visual proof passed 1/1 with 29 samples and 30 expected assertions, and the receipt reports positive native animations before reduced motion and zero reduced animations/errors/failed requests/HTTP errors/unexpected network.

Independent focused regression passed 31/31 domain/protocol/CLI tests. Sensitive scan passed with findingCount=0 across tracked/diff/index/worktree/untracked; private-ignore passed with targetCount=3, ignoredCount=3, trackedPrivateCount=0; protected-file diff and git diff --check passed.

Failure mode 1, cue/track drift or editor/CLI divergence — domain/CLI exact coverage and atomicity PASS, but editor adjustment parity FAILS because a valid stored-replacement Hold update is made unreachable.
Failure mode 2, hidden/missing canvas functionality or incorrect boundaries — Drag and visual boundaries PASS; Hold creation PASS; valid Hold enter-boundary adjustment FAILS in the filtered UI.

Failure mode 3, leakage or green tests masking runtime failures — privacy/runtime diagnostics PASS, but the green browser workflow masks the untested authored-Hold adjustment regression. Slice 3 and Phase 5 remain untouched.

parallel_safety.reason: The correction is one coupled editor behavior and installed-Chrome regression proof; splitting it would add coordination without creating a safely independent work package.

missing_evidence: An authored two-target Hold can change to another valid explicit source boundary without losing selected targets, then persist and reload with exact generated-target coverage.
An invalid edited enter boundary remains visibly unavailable or rejects atomically without corrupting the existing Hold, while returning to a valid boundary restores eligibility.
required_board_updates: Insert one bounded corrective Worker before T005. Objective: compute eligibility for an attached Hold from its stored source replacement so valid enter-boundary edits retain exact target coverage and invalid edits remain fail-closed.

Corrective verify: author the two-target Hold at 1000 ms; edit it to another valid explicit stored-source boundary; assert both selections remain, commit durably, reload, and prove semantic/generated target equality; exercise an invalid boundary and assert unchanged revision plus visible unavailability or rejection; restore a valid boundary; rerun installed Chrome twice for byte-identical receipts, focused suites, privacy scans, protected-file diff, and git diff --check.

Corrective stop_if: solving attached-Hold eligibility requires changing domain/protocol/compiler/runtime behavior, legacy cue bytes, private material, later-phase scope, or any file outside the two-file allowlist.
After correction, rerun this Judge gate before activating T005.
